correctness.rationale: The centered energy identity reduces dissipation to the symmetric circulant linearization. At equality, the polarized energy-preservation identity forces every nonzero zero-dissipation state to leave that set through the damped mean mode, so LaSalle leaves only the equilibrium. A positive-real-part linear mode gives the converse instability. The finite-dimensional Lorenz-96 endpoint formulas and algebraic identities were checked independently by symbolic/numerical residual tests.

originality.rationale: Kerin--Engler already prove the strict-interior global asymptotic stability criterion for homogeneous Lorenz-96-like G-maps, so that part is explicitly prior. The inspected Lorenz-96 stability and bifurcation literature did not state the marginal equality-case closure, the mean-transfer obstruction on the zero-dissipation subspace, or the resulting exact if-and-only-if global stability criterion. Because the endpoint proof is short and uses classical ingredients, an implicit or poorly indexed earlier observation remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Closing the nonhyperbolic boundary turns a strict sufficient energy condition into an exact global stability criterion for the homogeneous quadratic class. For standard Lorenz-96 it proves that the critical first linear threshold itself still has a globally attracting homogeneous equilibrium, excluding hidden finite-amplitude compact recurrence at the threshold.
